label: mid-sequence step right after t, with early 2/k first token (weak, conjunctive)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps) that fires only during the original phase or at the delimiter, at steps t=3..7 (orig_idx 4-5 carry about 65% of the mass), and never in the copy phase. It is strongly enriched when the previous input is t (18.9x lift, 54% of mass), and to a lesser degree 3 or x. It is also enriched when the token two steps back is t/3/x/g, when the first token is 2 or k (10x and 5.5x), when the current token is a first occurrence, and when the sequence has more digits. Top examples look like 2 3 t t [q] or k 2 n t t [1]: several t/3/x tokens just seen in a sequence that starts with 2 or k. Still, every combination of these cues is very imprecise, because most steps after t never fire. The best conjunction reaches only about 0.17-0.18 dev F1 and below 0.2 mass recall, so the trigger looks like a soft conjunction of hidden-state directions that no token predicate captures. Magnitude is highest in the top examples, which repeat t after a 2/k start, but I did not test this systematically.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=t (+5.22), orig0=2 (+4.38), prev2_tok=t (+4.28), prev_tok=3 (+3.91), prev2_tok=3 (+3.70), orig0=k (+3.66). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.26), prev3_tok=- (-2.57), in_first=0 (-0.66), n_digits=0 (-0.29).
